Q: Flutter web deployed on firebase is unable to receive any data though database streams A:

You’re actually very close, and the behavior you’re seeing is a classic Flutter Web + Firestore issue, not a Flutter bug.

The key point is this:

If Firestore access fails on Flutter Web, the stream does NOT error — it stays in ConnectionState.waiting forever.

That’s exactly what you’re observing.

Below is a clear explanation + checklist to fix it.

Why it works locally but hangs on Firebase Hosting

When you run locally:

  • You are usually logged in

  • Firestore rules may allow your local session

  • Emulator / cached auth can hide issues

When deployed:

  • The app runs as a public anonymous web user

  • Firestore rules + Firebase project config are enforced strictly

  • If Firestore denies the read, the stream never resolves

So the issue is NOT your StreamBuilder logic.

✅ Root Causes (most likely → least likely)

1️⃣ Firestore security rules (MOST COMMON CAUSE)

If Firestore rules require authentication, your deployed web app cannot read data.

On Flutter Web:

  • No auth

  • No error

  • Stream = ConnectionState.waiting forever

✅ Quick test (important)

Go to Firebase Console → Firestore → Rules and temporarily set:

service cloud.firestore {
  match /databases/{database}/documents {
    match /{document=**} {
      allow read: if true;
      allow write: if false;
    }
  }
}

Deploy again:

firebase deploy

👉 If data loads now, rules were the problem.

2️⃣ Authorized domains (if Auth is enabled)

If you use Firebase Authentication, your hosting domain must be whitelisted.

Check:

Firebase Console
→ Authentication
→ Settings
→ Authorized domains

Ensure these exist:

  • your-project.web.app

  • your-project.firebaseapp.com

  • Your custom domain (if any)

If missing → Firestore calls silently fail.

3️⃣ Firestore Web SDK requires indexed queries

Streaming a full collection without a limit is risky on web.

Always add a limit:

stream: FirebaseFirestore.instance
    .collection('events')
    .limit(50)
    .snapshots(),

This avoids:

  • Index failures

  • Large query hangs

  • Silent failures on web

4️⃣ Generic type mismatch (can break web builds)

Flutter Web is stricter than mobile.

This line can cause runtime JS crashes:

StreamBuilder<QuerySnapshot<Map<String, dynamic>>>

✅ Fix (recommended)

Let Firestore infer types:

StreamBuilder(
  stream: FirebaseFirestore.instance
      .collection('events')
      .limit(50)
      .snapshots(),
  builder: (context, snapshot) {

Or use a converter (best practice) 👇

5️⃣ Correct & future-proof solution: Use withConverter

This avoids web runtime errors entirely.

final eventsRef = FirebaseFirestore.instance
    .collection('events')
    .withConverter<EventData>(
      fromFirestore: (snapshot, _) =>
          EventData.fromJson(snapshot.data()!),
      toFirestore: (event, _) => event.toJson(),
    );

StreamBuilder<QuerySnapshot<EventData>>(
  stream: eventsRef.limit(50).snapshots(),
  builder: (context, snapshot) {
    if (snapshot.hasError) {
      return Text(snapshot.error.toString());
    }
    if (!snapshot.hasData) {
      return const CircularProgressIndicator();
    }

    return Text(snapshot.data!.docs.first.data().toString());
  },
);

This is the most stable setup for Flutter Web.

Why you see 200 OK but still fail

Firestore Web SDK uses:

  • WebSockets

  • IndexedDB

  • gRPC-Web

So:

  • Network tab shows 200

  • Browser console throws JS errors

  • Flutter stream never completes

This is expected behavior when:

  • Rules block access

  • Domain isn’t authorized

  • Data type mapping fails

✅ Debug checklist (follow in order)

  1. Temporarily allow public reads → test

  2. Add .limit() to query

  3. Remove generic Map typing

  4. Use withConverter()

  5. Check authorized domains

  6. Redeploy hosting

Final Answer (TL;DR)

Your stream hangs on Firebase Hosting because Firestore access is blocked or mismatched on Flutter Web, and Firestore Web does not throw readable errors — it stays in ConnectionState.waiting.

✔ Fix Firestore rules
✔ Limit queries
✔ Remove strict Map typing
✔ Use withConverter()

Once you do that, the stream will work exactly like it does locally.

Q: Correct type hint error thrown by PHPStan on UserInterface in Symfony project A:

I think you at least got whats the problem: The return type of the method getUser is @return UserInterface|object|null while createMapMarker expects an instance of UserInterface.

Before calling createMapMarker you should check that the return value of getUser is actually an instance of UserInterface and probably a simple /** @var UserInterface $user */ right on top the the $user variable declaration will fix.
